headline: US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has backed AI as a way for Americans to check their own medical advice, which has divided his own supporters and drawn criticism from medical experts.
score_reason: Senior official's policy stance on AI in health with broad reach, but it is an opinion and political story, not a new rule.
importance_line: Patients, doctors and the MAHA movement are affected by the health secretary's push for AI as a check on medical advice; the experts quoted dispute his reasoning and no policy change is announced.
summary: The Associated Press reports that Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. told a recent 'Make America Healthy Again' (MAHA) summit that AI would let Americans 'fact check their own medical advice', a stance that some MAHA allies call corporate-friendly and that bioethicist Zeke Emanuel says misunderstands how AI works. An HHS spokesperson responded that Kennedy wants AI to help people understand their health data and give doctors more time, while the AP notes that OpenAI and Anthropic were among the summit's paying sponsors.
notes: AP page blocked here; text read from AP wire copy on ABC News. Kept as HEA (could be POL).
